payload.goal: Cut the time a resuming session spends re-orienting before its first real action. The SessionStart digest already carries a file-locality hint (speed T4) but it renders as 29 initiative-wide absolute paths polluted with dead scratchpad temp files, so agents ignore it and re-grep the source for type shapes instead. Make the hint task-scoped, repo-relative and free of non-repo paths, then decide whether the record should carry what the next session needs to KNOW (interface shapes) and not merely where it lives.

payload.text:
EVIDENCE — user screenshot, 2026-08-30, Claude Code v2.1.251, Opus 5 1M, xhigh effort, session-driver 8/11. User typed "continue". Model answered "I'll pick up where the last session left off. Let me start the session and orient." then immediately ran `sed -n '40,120p' packages/engine/src/core/fold.ts; echo '=== PlanTaskInput ==='; sed -n '55,110p' packages/schema/src/events.ts`. Status line at that moment: Puttering 28s, 1.7k tokens down, ctx 8%, cache 97%.

READ THE NUMBERS BEFORE BLAMING THE RECORD. ctx 8% and cache 97% mean context was nearly EMPTY and the cache was warm — neither record size nor cache misses can explain 28 seconds. Two things can: xhigh reasoning effort spending a large thinking budget on a turn where the record had already decided what to do, and the orientation read the model performed because the digest did not give it what it needed. Only the second is sofar's problem, and the first is probably the larger share. Do not optimise the digest expecting to recover the 28s.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT, verified by rendering `sofar status` on this repo. The file-locality hint from speed T4 exists, and its own source comment in projections/templates/status.ts promises "where the ACTIVE TASK's work actually lives ... one budgeted line". What renders instead is:
  Files touched (29):
  - /Users/jins/IO/sofar/CLAUDE.md
  ... 28 more ...
Three separate faults, each independently worth fixing:
1. NON-REPO PATHS ARE RECORDED AND RENDERED. The list includes /private/tmp/claude-501/<session>/scratchpad/commit-1.1.txt, commit-1.2.txt and runtime-comparison.html. These are session-scoped temp files that are already gone and can never be useful to any future session. They are guaranteed-dead paths occupying digest budget.
2. ABSOLUTE PATHS. /Users/jins/IO/sofar/ repeats on every repo line — pure token waste, and it leaks the operator's machine layout into a record that gets committed and synced.
3. INITIATIVE-WIDE, NOT TASK-SCOPED. 29 files across an 11-task initiative carries no signal about which task is next, so an agent correctly ignores it and greps instead. The comment says active task; the behaviour says whole initiative.

WHY THE FIX IS ONLY HALF THE ANSWER. The model did not grep to learn WHERE the code was — it grepped a specific line range hunting the shape of PlanTaskInput. Paths answer where; the model needed what. A perfect file hint would still have left it reading source. That makes this the first concrete, measured use case for the agent-emitted enrichment layer proposed in roadmap-h2: the session that just finished task 7 knows exactly which type shapes task 8 needs, and could say so for a few output tokens, where the next session pays a multi-thousand-token read to rediscover it. Prefer this as the pilot for that layer over anything abstract — it has an observed cost and an obvious success metric, namely whether the resuming session's first action is real work rather than a grep.

CONCURRENCY WARNING, do not skip. A peer session is live on session-driver (statusline showed 8/11, and the digest's own concurrent-edits warning lists it) and projections/templates/status.ts is among the files touched by this initiative's recent work. Do NOT begin editing status.ts or fold.ts from a second session while that peer is running. Coordinate first or wait; this repo has already been burned by concurrent write-backs.

payload.next_action: Before any code, tell the user the two non-sofar wins that cost nothing: drop reasoning effort from xhigh to high or medium for resume-and-execute turns, since xhigh is being spent re-deciding what the record already decided, and clear the MCP server authentication warning shown in the screenshot. Then, only once the peer session on session-driver has finished, make the file-locality hint task-scoped, repo-relative and filtered of non-repo paths in projections/templates/status.ts, and pilot the roadmap-h2 enrichment layer by having a finishing session record the type shapes the next task needs.

payload.text:
ADDING AN EVENT TYPE — the eight touch points, in order. Derived empirically from commit bacbb86 (session-driver 1.2, three driver events); every session that adds an event type currently rediscovers this by grepping a 1463-line fold.ts and a 683-line events.ts, which is minutes of archaeology per session.

1. docs/SPEC.md — contract FIRST; SPEC is authoritative over improvisation, so the envelope/payload shape lands here before code.
2. packages/schema/src/events.ts — payload interface plus the entry in the event union. This is the ONLY schema home (guard-rail); nothing outside packages/schema/src may define payloads.
3. packages/schema/test/schema.test.ts — validation coverage for the new payload.
4. packages/engine/src/core/fold.ts — a case in applyEvent's switch (31 cases as of 2026-08-30) plus any InitiativeState fields the event folds into. Note the ordering hazard already in the file: some derivations must run BEFORE applyEvent because they need the plan as it stands.
5. packages/engine/src/projections/templates/shared.ts — shared render helpers, if the event surfaces in more than one projection.
6. packages/engine/src/projections/templates/session.ts — session-file rendering.
7. packages/engine/src/projections/templates/status.ts — the SessionStart digest. Anything a future session must see at orientation goes here or it is invisible in practice.
8. packages/engine/test/<feature>-events.test.ts — a dedicated test file; the driver events shipped 219 lines of it.

Then `npm run build`, because of the trap already recorded above in this file: the in-session MCP tools run the GLOBAL install and will reject a payload type it does not know. To write events using the new type before publishing, bypass MCP and use the freshly built local engine — `node packages/engine/dist/cli.js event append <slug> --type … --payload …`.

Templates 5-7 are the ones most often missed, and missing them is silent: the event folds correctly and simply never appears in any projection, so the record looks complete while the next session cannot see the thing you recorded.

If archaeology persists, the next candidates are the same treatment for other recurring shapes, a projection-template recipe and a hook recipe, before touching any code. The file-locality hint faults recorded earlier still stand but are now clearly the second priority, and still must wait for the peer session on session-driver to finish before status.ts is edited.
payload.summary: Second screenshot of the same stalled session revised the diagnosis and produced the actual fix. Two minutes later the same resume had gone from 28 seconds and 1.7k tokens to 2 minutes 29 seconds and 8.6k tokens, context only 8 to 10 percent and cache 97 to 98 percent, and the model was on its SECOND exploratory read of the same file, first sed on fold.ts and events.ts, then grep for plan_updated and task_added with 25 lines of context. So this is not one grep and it is not primarily reasoning effort as I said last time: it is serial code archaeology across a 1463-line fold.ts and a 683-line events.ts, and my earlier split that called xhigh the larger share was wrong. The model was not lost about WHERE code lives, which is what the file-locality hint addresses; it was reconstructing HOW this repo adds an event type, which no artifact in the record carries. Verified the gap: repo.md documents the event-type GOTCHA, that in-session MCP tools run the global install and reject an unknown payload type until rebuild, but carries no map of where the code goes, which is backwards from what a resuming session needs first. Derived the recipe empirically from commit bacbb86 rather than guessing, and wrote it to repo memory as the eight touch points in order: SPEC first, then schema events plus its test, fold applyEvent whose switch is at 31 cases, the three projection templates shared, session and status, and a dedicated test file. Recorded that templates 5 through 7 are the commonly missed ones and that missing them fails silently, since the event folds correctly and simply never renders, so the record looks complete while the next session cannot see it. This reframes roadmap-h2 item 5: the cheapest wins in serving each agent its piece are CONVENTIONS, not indexes, and they cost nothing and need no ruling.
